Threshold
The six conditions
Condition — Requirement
Ijāza — Take permission from one who holds authorisation.
Diet — Abstain from animal products, both jamālī and jalālī .
Dress — Unstitched cloth — newly washed, or as one wears iḥrām .
Retreat — Fast, and sit in iʿtikāf in the masjid facing the qibla. If wuḍūʾ breaks, renew it and complete the recitation — a wuḍūʾ ʿalā'l-fawr , not a break in the count.
Water — River water for eating, drinking, wuḍūʾ and ghusl.
Food — Bread of Lahori salt, kneaded with river water in a state of wuḍūʾ, cooked over a wood fire — with care that the wood carry no insects.
The three grades
All three arrive at the same reckoning by different routes. The bars below show duration; the figures give the daily count.
Followed by ṣadaqa of a cow or a chicken, according to means. Alternative form: fast Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; each day after ghusl pray two rakʿas nafl, then recite 120.
Ṣadaqa of one chicken per day, plus cash daily if able. Conditioned on a daʿwat of the middling kind.
Some hold it may be completed in six days at the same daily reckoning.
After the zakāt
Recite the Ḥizb once after ṣalāt if possible, otherwise afterwards. Fajr, ʿAṣr and Maghrib are specified as the times not to be missed.

Where the practitioner has completed the ṣaghīr route by the six-day reckoning, the compiler still requires at least one recitation daily after ʿAṣr, with permanent abstention from beef. Some shaykhs, he notes, do not require the beef restriction even for this.
Directing a specific need
This is the master rule that generates every entry in Part III:

When a need arises, take the one phrase of the Ḥizb that corresponds to the object — matched to a divine Name, an ism-i ilāhī , or an appropriate āya — and append it seventy times at the end of that phrase. Begin the Ḥizb from the start, holding the intention in mind, and on reaching that phrase recite it in the manner described.
During recitation one turns toward the rūḥ-i mubārak of the Imām.
Method — the ishārāt
The sequence
Opening breath The ḥurūf-i khamsī (ا ب ت ث ٹ) from beginning to end on a single breath . Hold the image of Imām Abū'l-Ḥasan al-Shādhilī and seek his imdād . In the litany ↑

At sakhkhir lanā hādhā'l-baḥr Bring the object of the request to mind. Repeat, closing a finger of the right hand at each letter; recite kāhāyāʿaynṣād three times. Hand faces forward. Hold the intention of kushāyish — opening, expansion. See the finger map below. In the litany ↑
At wa'ṭmis … lā yastaṭīʿūna'l-muḍiyya wa lā'l-majīʾa ilaynā Gesture with the right hand toward the enemies, shayāṭīn and the like held in mind. In the litany ↑
At shāhati'l-wujūh Recite three times, each time striking the hand straight down toward the earth. Envisage the destruction of the adversaries. In the litany ↑
The seven ḥā-mīms Six directions, then the seventh into the hands. See the orientation diagram below. In the litany ↑
At kāhāyāʿaynṣād kifāyatunā Close the fingers and recite kifāyatunā , straightening the hand opposite each letter. In the litany ↑
At ḥāmīm ʿaynsīnqāf ḥimāyatunā Close the fingers and recite ḥimāyatunā , continuing to fa-sayakfīkahumu'llāh — then open the hands.

Khawāṣṣ — sixty-four operations

Sixty-four operations. Each is a phrase lifted from the Ḥizb , joined to a divine Name matched to the purpose, and given a count. Two patterns run through the catalogue: the standing ×70 append , and — later in the catalogue — a regimen , in which the whole Ḥizb is recited a set number of times daily for a set number of days, with the appended formula inserted ×70 on reaching the designated phrase. The pattern is marked on each entry.

Each operation is a phrase of the Ḥizb joined to a divine Name and given a count — and the count sits on that joined formula, not on the litany line as it passes. Where an entry gives two counts, the larger is the whole Ḥizb’s and the seventy is the formula’s.

Nothing else is attached. The zakāt of Part V stands over the catalogue as a whole and the ishārāt of Part VI belong to reciting the Ḥizb; neither is repeated on the individual entries, and neither should be read into one that does not mention it.

title: 53 Goitre ×3, or ×1 over each of seven lumps
formula: The whole Ḥizb
method: (1) A black ḥarmal seed, broken slightly; recite the Ḥizb over it three times; give morning, midday and evening. (2) Seven lumps of Lahori salt equal in size to the swelling; recite the Ḥizb once over each. The patient dissolves one lump in water daily for seven days, with the intention that as the lump dissolves so the swelling will go.

title: 54 Undoing siḥr — obstinate cases ×3, three Tuesdays
formula: The whole Ḥizb over sea-water
method: Recite on a Tuesday; have the patient bathe with it. Repeat for three Tuesdays.

title: 55 Protection of the house — the door inscription written
formula: shāhati'l-wujūh ×3 · wa ʿanati'l-wujūhu li'l-ḥayyi'l-qayyūm · wa qad khāba man ḥamala ẓulmā
method: Write and affix at the door.

title: 56 Residual jinn-effects ×13
formula: The whole Ḥizb over oil
method: Where jinn have been driven off but pain remains in the body: apply the oil to the site of the pain and to all the nails.

title: 57 Every need — the tested practice 700 daily, 7 days
formula: yā Allāhu anta rabbī, yā Allāhu anta ḥasbī
method: Daily nisāb 700: 500 standing, 100 sitting, 100 lying. Best at tahajjud. No dietary restriction; wuḍūʾ and facing the qibla required. There may be light, or none. Useful for every purpose in dīn and dunyā, and especially in a particular calamity, a specific danger, or a court case.
lim: Niẓāmī is explicit: this is not to be recited by proxy. The person whose affair it is must recite it himself.

title: 58 Lifting a calamity ×1,100 within the night
formula: unṣurnā fa-innaka khayru'l-nāṣirīn
method: No fixed nisāb or zakāt. When calamity or the fear of it falls on someone, he, his wife, children and gathered friends recite it. If they wish, the whole may be completed in a single night, and the affliction lifts.

title: 59 Expansion of provision — the four quarters ×123 daily, 4 days
formula: waftaḥ lanā fa-innaka khayru'l-fātiḥīn
method: From after Fajr until sunrise. The duʿā has 23 letters, eleven dotted and twelve undotted. Day 1 facing east; day 2 west; day 3 south; day 4 north. On the fourth day, a quarter- bhar of raisins and a quarter- bhar of dried chickpeas are offered as niyāz to Khwāja Khiḍr; the chickpeas are distributed and the practitioner eats a few of the raisins. By the seventh day the effects appear. Open to men, women, Muslim and non-Muslim alike; no precautions required during it.

title: 60 Increase of provision and blessing in trade ×122 daily, 1st to 21st of the month
formula: wa'rzuqnā fa-innaka khayru'l-rāziqīn
method: After ʿIshāʾ. Has a zakāt. No abstentions beyond the ordinary — all lawful food permitted. Several people may perform it together, and it may be recited on another's behalf.

title: 61 Blessing at the door written once
formula: Bismi'llāhi bābunā
method: Written on stone, metal or paper and fixed at the door of the house; brings great blessing and keeps affliction from that house. No ʿamal or nisāb is required. It may be written by any practitioner of the Ḥizb, or by anyone who has permission — and the compiler adds that permission from himself is also given.

title: 62 Offspring — the apple ×9 daily, 9 days
formula: ḥāʾ mīm, al-amru wa jāʾa'l-naṣr
method: After Maghrib, from the new moon to the full moon. Keep an apple before you, recite the ʿamal nine times, breathe on the apple; then have the wife eat half and the husband half — the apple is not to be peeled, though the seeds are removed. Hold the intention throughout: that if a child is not born, God grant a child; if born but not surviving, God let it live; if a daughter, God grant a son.

title: 63 Rafīq-i nisvāṇ — for women ×101 each night, 21 nights
formula: sitru'l-ʿarshi masbūlun ʿalaynā
method: After ʿIshāʾ, without a break. For distress from a husband, from parents, from in-laws, from disobedient children, or from the difficulties that arise on a husband's death. Because of the interruption of the monthly days, begin on a date such that the 21 fall clear. No dietary restriction; the single binding condition is that the time and the place of the first night be kept identical for all 21 nights , or the ʿamal yields nothing.
lim: He states there is no danger of rujʿat in it, although it is a muwakkal operation, because the angels appointed to it are attached to the ʿArsh-i Aʿẓam; women who perform it may see them in dream and receive good counsel. Perform wuḍūʾ before reciting, keep fragrance present, and light if desired. Once the nisāb is discharged, thereafter ×18 suffices for any particular purpose — the words of the ʿamal being eighteen letters — and one asks of God after the eighteen.

title: 64 Dafʿ-i zahr — poison, the evil eye and siḥr ×7 at sunrise, ×7 at zawāl, ×7 at sunset · 40 days
formula: bismi'llāhi'lladhī lā yaḍurru maʿa'smihī shayʾ
method: The practitioner stands, with both hands immersed in water up to the wrists. Forty days, unbroken. No dietary restriction and no other procedure. Once the nisāb is complete, a single recitation breathed onto water or food is enough: given to the afflicted person to drink or eat, it lifts the evil eye and the siḥr and draws off the poison. If a healthy person performs it continuously for seven days, neither the evil eye nor siḥr nor poison will affect him.

Apparatus — the thirteen khawāṣṣ
The thirteen khawāṣṣ

Whoever recites it at sunrise — Allāh accepts his supplication, removes his distress, raises his rank and station among people, opens his breast to tawḥīd, makes his affairs easy, turns his straitness into expansion, keeps him secure from the evil of jinn and men, and protects him from the calamities of earth and heaven.
And the Imām's own word: "Had my Ḥizb been recited in Baghdad, it would not have been taken."
The house in which my Ḥizb is recited remains protected from calamities and afflictions.
Whoever recites it to be safe from the harm of a tyrant remains safe from that harm.

Whoever recites it daily after every prayer remains protected from the events of the age, becomes self-sufficient, and finds religious and worldly felicity present in his every movement and stillness.
Whoever recites it in the first hour of Friday remains in safety from afflictions.
The house in which it is recited remains safe from burning.
A corpse upon which it is written and hung remains safe from becoming the morsel of wild beasts and birds.
Whoever recites it in the first hour of Friday — Allāh casts love of him into people's hearts.
Whoever wishes to attain his aim: after Fajr let him recite Sūra Yā Sīn ten times , then this duʿā seventy times , and Allāh will fulfil his aim.
Whoever holds regularly to this Ḥizb will be protected from sudden death — from drowning, from lightning, from burning in fire.
If a ship's wind is contrary, let this Ḥizb be recited and by Allāh's command a favourable wind will come at once.
If this duʿā is written on the walls surrounding a city, or on the walls of a house, that city, house or dwelling will be preserved from accidents and calamities.
In wars this duʿā has great importance.
It is a duʿā of dominance and victory against every opponent.
The Ḥizb al-Baḥr is a promise-keeping shield of protection; for those beginning the road of sulūk it carries asrār-i shāfī , and for those at the end, lights of utter purity.

The opening breath Working book The working book opens its ishārāt at the naming of the letters: they are taken from beginning to end on a single breath, the image of the Imām held before the heart and his imdād sought. One caution about the join — the compiler writes ḥurūf-i khamsī and gives ا ب ت ث ٹ, the head of the Urdu alphabet, where the recital above sets out the twenty-eight Arabic ḥurūf . Reading the one instruction onto the other list is editorial, not his. The Sharḥ has no gesture at this place. Working book · the hand The opening breath. The ḥurūf are taken from beginning to end on a single breath , holding the image of Imām Abū’l-Ḥasan al-Shādhilī and seeking his imdād . This is the first station of the ishārāt.
